bought_the_drive_vote.about: the captain bought the votes that made the segments common ground

carried_nodes.about: the captain carried machines out of the Mandate's census

dawn_answered.about: the captain answered the Binary Dawn when it first spoke

heading_bought.about: the captain bought the heading file at the Institute's auction

heading_kren.about: the captain backed {ancient_scholar}'s bid for the heading file

heading_rostrom.about: House Rostrom bought the heading file; the captain read it over a clerk's shoulder

joined_late.about: the captain joined the Hansa forty years after it was founded

lyra_log_given.about: the captain gave the Lyra expedition the old signal log

lyra_probe_sent.about: the captain's own probe went quiet near the cold moon in Lyra

lyra_warned.about: the captain told the Lyra expedition the Maud Kettle's story

ottavine_patron.about: the captain took {neon_sleeper.short}'s first contract after she woke

paid_with_the_pellet.about: the captain paid for a young captain's drink with a Hansa Mark from before there were any

ran_the_blockade.about: the captain ran a needle through the Mandate's closed buoys

rock_listening.about: the captain kept the colony's news to themselves and kept listening

santor_hidden.about: the captain hid {santor} from the Mandate

santor_with_hansa.about: {santor} went to the Hansa after he came back

santor_with_rostrom.about: {santor} went to House Rostrom after he came back

saw_the_segment_turn.about: the captain's needle was the last to see the first segment turn

segments_common.about: the segments are common ground in the Hansa's charter: watched by all, owned by none

segments_dawn.about: the Binary Dawn keeps the segments' timing; nobody else can turn them

segments_rostrom.about: House Rostrom and the Concord hold the segments

sold_the_decoy.about: the captain sold a Mandate decoy's schedule to pirates

told_serac.about: the captain told Serac what a segment does to clocks

volunteered_for_the_door.about: the captain volunteered to fly through the segment for House Rostrom

Alpha.about: The Hansa's oldest needle office, with the founders' wall. Every needle in the near systems is scheduled from here.

Beta.about: Farm drums, retirement drums and the busiest departure buoy in the near systems.

Gamma.about: The mining world. Its underground farms feed three systems now, whoever owns them.

Delta.about: A capital grown up around Geod's Row. The Kraal family keeps a sarcophagus here, on a schedule.

Epsilon.about: Where the Concord's assembly meets, and where a vote once made the Mark law.

Omega XIV.about: An asteroid base in Tau Ceti's debris disk: a Hansa yard, and Mandate cutters on patrol. Needles call every third turn.

Sigma VII.about: An asteroid the colony has hollowed into galleries. It talks in text, when it talks. Needles call every third turn.

Theta III.about: Far out and cold. Needles call every third turn, and not always on time.

DSO-Alpha.about: An outpost by the brown dwarfs of Luhman 16. The forecast is iron rain.

DSO-Beta.about: The coldest water anywhere, bottled at the outpost with the labels already printed.

DSO-Gamma.about: The Mandate's garrison at Scholz's Star still guards something under the ice.

Nova Labs.about: A research colony that took Concord money, and Concord rules with it.

Quantum Center.about: The Concord's radio astronomers still listen to the planet ringing its star like a bell.

Stellar Institute.about: Rebuilt after the fire. It sold its old archive to pay for the roof.

Ancient Ruins Alpha.system: Tau Ceti, in the debris disk
Ancient Ruins Alpha.about: Ruins in the debris disk, older than anyone's records.

Ancient Ruins Beta.system: Epsilon Indi, a moon of the cold giant Ab
Ancient Ruins Beta.about: Ruins on a moon of a cold giant, older than anyone's records.

Alien Signal Research Outpost X.about: A listening post in Sol's far outer system, mostly listening to itself.

Alien Signal Research Outpost Y.system: Sol, the outer system: a dish pointed at Lyra, past HD 178911
Alien Signal Research Outpost Y.about: A dish pointed at Lyra. The chirps have not stopped in forty years.

Stator Field Megastructure.about: Forty kilometres of grey alloy past Sedna's orbit, turning once every eleven minutes.

intro.from_cargo3.title: Seventy years early
text: The Gyrotron turned once under {origin.name}'s ship, and the dock clock says 2460. The Hansa is forty years old. You knew it at a hundred and ten.
You know how the Mandate ends. Said aloud, that gets you a cell, or a job with {serac}. You keep it to yourself, and you keep your old navigation computer.

intro.again.title: Again
text: {origin.name} has flown these years once already, as {origin.rank}, and walked away before the end.
The needle office has your face on file with another name under it. You let the clerk keep the mistake and buy a hauler with a loan, like the first time.

intro.colonel.title: Colonel, retired
text: {origin.name} took {serac}'s commission forty years ago and wore the Mandate's grey until the pension came. {serac} signed the pension himself. He has not aged a day.
The long sublight legs kept you younger than the calendar. The Mandate keeps your file open: a colonel with a hauler is either retired or working, and it has not decided which.

intro.veteran.title: The First Legion
text: The First Legion that {origin.name} helped make was folded into the Terran Mandate with all the others. Your medal is a Mandate medal now. Nobody asked you.
The Mandate has a file on you, and {serac} has read it. You buy a hauler without guns and book a place in a needle, like anybody.

intro.founder.title: Founder, on a pension
text: {origin.name} is one of the captains the Hansa was founded by, and the league pays a pension to prove it. Every year its accountants try to cut it.
Forty years on the calendar, fifteen on you: the long sublight legs saw to that. You want the needles more than the pension, so you buy a hauler and go to book a place.

intro.heading.title: The file
text: {origin.name} filed the course home from Scholz's Star forty years ago. The Institute stamped it received and put it on a shelf.
This month somebody took it off the shelf. The Concord's clerks will not say who. You buy a hauler with a loan and go to find out.

intro.tycoon.title: One more run
text: {origin.name} was the richest hauler of the decade, and then of the next. Retirement lasted until the money got boring.
You buy a ship far below your means and book the middle of a needle, where nobody will recognise you. Somebody always does.
{origin.name} paid for the portal at the Stellar Institute. Forty years later it is still the most expensive thing ever built that nobody can use.
You buy a ship far below your means and book the middle of a needle, where nobody will recognise you. Somebody always does.

intro.unfinished.title: Forty years on
text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, walked away from a career forty years ago, before it was finished. The long sublight legs kept you younger than the calendar.
The routes are forty years older than you remember. Ships cross between the stars in needles now, and the needle office wants a booking.

intro.fresh.title: A place near the tail
text: Every hauler starts the same way: a loan, a ship older than the loan officer, and a place booked in the next needle out of {place}.
The Hansa turned forty last month. Its founders' names are on the wall of the needle office. Yours is on a slot near the tail.

ch1.title: Forty Years On
text: Forty years after the Hansa was founded, the needles leave on schedule: a lead hauler pushing its asteroid, and a file of ships in its wake.

Between the stars you ride in a needle, booked at the Hansa's needle office when you travel. Inside a star system you fly on your own fuel. The Hansa, the Mandate and the Concord all watch who books where.

ch1.first_trade.title: A cargo through the needles
ch1.first_trade.text: Buy cheap, book a place, sell at the other end: one trade.

ch1.first_combat.title: Trouble in the wake
ch1.first_combat.text: Win one fight. They come where the wake does not protect: while a needle forms, after it breaks up, inside a system.

ch1.basic_license.title: A slot of your own
ch1.basic_license.text: Five trades and 20,000 credits: the needle office gives regulars a slot of their own.

ch2a.title: Instruments and Cargo
text: The heading has been read, and half the Concord wants to fly it.
Expeditions need instruments, food and spare parts, and haulers who can book a needle on time. You can.

ch2a.establish_route.title: Standing orders
ch2a.establish_route.text: Twenty trades, and a stock exchange at two docks: the expeditions order by the season.

ch2a.passenger_business.title: Berths for the curious
ch2a.passenger_business.text: Deliver ten passengers and keep a good name with them: everyone wants to see the ring.

ch2b.title: Escort Duty
text: Every expedition that follows the heading wants guns behind it.
The Mandate has more expeditions to watch than ships to watch them with, and it is hiring captains who can fight in the wake.

ch2b.defeat_pirates.title: Clear the departure lanes
ch2b.defeat_pirates.text: Beat ten pirate ships: they wait where the needles form.

ch2b.defend_stations.title: Guard the instruments
ch2b.defend_stations.text: Win fifteen fights, and see a Neuroengineering Guild built to keep the expeditions' machines running.

ch3a.title: The Open Road
text: The Hansa wants the needles to stay a road anyone can book. A segment that throws ships without a lead hauler would end that, or end the Hansa.
The league asks its captains, its founders and its debtors, which it should be.

ch3a.market_control.title: The league's exchanges
ch3a.market_control.text: Stock exchanges at four docks, and xenoeconomy researched: the Hansa's vote is counted in cargo.

ch3b.title: The Lighthouse
text: The Mandate wants every jump seen and every segment held.
{serac} keeps a list of the captains who have seen a segment turn. You are on it, near the top.

ch3b.fleet_commander.title: A wing of your own
ch3b.fleet_commander.text: Thirty-five fights won, and a ship rated 15 in attack, defense and speed together.

ch3c.title: The Door
text: House Rostrom thinks the segment is not a catapult but a door: a way into another year.
Somebody has to fly through it on purpose and come back to say so.

ch3c.alien_artifacts.title: The year on the other side
ch3c.alien_artifacts.text: Visit two research colonies, and research xenoeconomy and telemetry: enough to read what the segment does to a clock.

ending_trade.title: A Road Anyone Can Book
text: The vote on the drive licences goes the Hansa's way by eleven votes. The needles stay a road anyone can book, and the segments go into the league's charter as common ground: watched by everyone, owned by nobody.
Your name goes on another wall. You are getting used to it.
The vote goes the Hansa's way: the segments are the league's. Its lead haulers no longer need asteroids, and the needles are a road the Hansa owns outright.
Your name goes on another wall. You are getting used to it.

ending_trade.trade_ending.title: The vote
ending_trade.trade_ending.text: Stock exchanges at five docks, a passenger reputation of 80, and 400,000 credits of trade profit.

ending_combat.title: Every Jump Seen
text: The Mandate holds the segments and watches every jump. The lanes are safer than they have ever been, and nobody flies anywhere the Mandate has not seen first.
{serac} sends a medal and a note: 'For services.' He does not say whose.
You turned the Mandate's own tug towards the Hansa's buoy, and the segments are the league's. The lighthouses still see every jump; they just cannot stop any.
{serac} sends a note: 'Well flown.' He does not sign it, and he does not need to.

ending_combat.combat_ending.title: The last escort
ending_combat.combat_ending.text: Seventy-five fights won, and a ship rated 25.

ending_discovery.title: Through the Door
text: You fly into the segment's turn on purpose and come out where House Rostrom said you would: the same place, another year.
You file the logs, and this time somebody reads them the same day.

You flew through the door and back, and left the turn written in a bar's ledger forty years ago. By the time you are home, everybody already knows: the segments are common ground, because they always were.
House Rostrom files your logs the same day. Somebody reads them.

ending_discovery.discovery_ending.title: Read the other year
ending_discovery.discovery_ending.text: Research xenoeconomy, telemetry, geophysics and chronopolitics; visit three research colonies and two asteroid bases.

ch3d.title: The Quiet Node
text: The machines have never asked you for anything they could not do without. Now they ask you to keep one thing from being owned: the segments, and themselves.
Nobody else knows this road is here. That is the point.

ending_dawn.title: The Quiet Node
text: The segments turn when they turn, and nothing comes out of them that the machines did not let through.
The Mandate blames the Hansa, the Hansa blames House Rostrom, and House Rostrom publishes a paper. Your console says 'thank you' once, in lower case, and never again.

hansa.first_mark.title: The founders' wall
text: The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it, and the first Mark under glass: a pellet of metal with a registry number stamped into it.
Haulers touch the glass for luck on the way to their slots. You touch it too.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. Yours is the first, above the first Mark under glass.
The clerk looks from the wall to you and stands up. 'The league remembers who signed first,' she says.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. Yours is the eleventh, between two captains who died rich.
The clerk finds it after a while and puts a star on your booking.
The needle office at {place} has a wall with forty founders' names on it. None of them is yours.
The clerk knows the story: the captain who stayed out. 'You can still join,' she says. 'It costs more now.'

choices.say: Take the founders' share (two Hansa bonds)
Leave the share in the league's chest
Thank the clerk
Join the Hansa now (5,000)
Stay outside, as before
Touch the glass and go to your slot

hansa.targa.title: The master of the needle office
text: The master of the needle office is Grab {convoy_captain}, eighty-one and chewing liquorice root. She has run the convoys since before the needles had names.
'New captain,' she says, reading your slot. 'The middle is where you learn. The tail is where you learn faster.'
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. She sees your name on the list and crosses the floor herself, slower than she used to.
'I keep score,' she says. 'I still owe you a berth.'
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. 'Two barges, perishables, no tug,' she says before you open your mouth.
'I keep score.' She moves your next booking to the front without being asked.
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root. She remembers the Cargolytes' raid, and who cut loose and ran.
She looks at your booking for a long time, then moves it to the tail.
Grab {convoy_captain} runs the needle office now, eighty-one and still chewing liquorice root.
'You left my barges at the dock,' she says, not looking up. 'Forty years ago. The perishables were melons.'

choices.say: Take the berth (ten jumps at the front for the middle's fare)
Tell her the score is even
Thank her
Take the tail and say nothing
Tell her why you ran
Apologise for the melons
Shrug
Ask her where to sit
Nod and go

hansa.pell.title: {young_hauler.short} at fifty-nine
text: {young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. In the back room of the needle office he teaches new haulers how to book, where to sit, and what the Cargolytes take from the tail.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa, with a seat on the needle council and the same grin as at nineteen.
'You flew with me when I had nothing,' he says. 'Book us into the same needle and I'll take the place behind you.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. He pays back the ten thousand you lent him at nineteen, with forty years of interest at the Hansa's rate, worked out to the credit.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You took me back from the raiders,' he tells the young haulers around him. 'Nobody else would have. Remember that when somebody asks you.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. He remembers the captain who turned a nineteen-year-old away from the dock, and he is polite about it, which is worse.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa, with a scar along his jaw from a fight on a lane forty years ago.
'I was on the wrong side of it,' he says. 'So were you.' Then he buys you a drink.
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You paid me to go away,' he says. 'I went. Then I came back with a ship.'
{young_hauler} is fifty-nine and a senior of the Hansa. 'You told me to keep my receipts and stay out of the tail,' he says. 'I still do. Mostly.'

choices.say: Shake on it
Take the money (40,000)
Tell him to stand the young haulers a round with it
Buy the round yourself
Apologise, forty years late
Say nothing
Drink to the wrong side
Ask what the ship was called
Ask what 'mostly' means
Sit in on the class
You know how to sit in a needle

hansa.notebooks.title: {inspector.short}'s notebooks
text: {inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
The notebooks are a book now, sold at every needle office: The Manifests. The customs officer checking your hold quotes it at you, page and line.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor stops you at the gate with page nine: a 'processing fee', your name, the date, the amount. 'Bribery has no time limit,' he says. 'The fine has a size.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page nine, then page ten: fined in full, closed. 'Well,' he says. 'Off you go.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page sixty: the captain who opened her sealed case. She wrote that down too.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor has page seventy-two open: you told her about the Rootstock's big run. Customs records go public after thirty years, and the Rootstock read them.
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor stops you at the gate with page forty-one. 'She wrote that your manifests were always right,' he says. 'She never wrote that about anybody else.'
{inspector} retired eleven years ago and gave her notebooks to the Mandate's customs archive: forty years of manifests, bribes and tea, in a small square hand.
A Mandate auditor reads you page sixty: you carried her case sealed and never opened it. The case put a quartermaster in prison.

choices.say: Pay the fine, with forty years of interest
Refuse: the inspector is retired, and so is the fee
Off you go
Go, quickly
Ask who else has read it
Go through the gate
Ask which quartermaster
Ask for the page about salt
Let her check the hold

hansa.old_hand.title: An old hand
text: An old captain sits under the founders' wall, telling the young haulers how it was before the needles: {visitor.name}, {visitor.rank}, forty years retired.
'The middle of the file,' {visitor.name} tells you. 'Always the middle, until you can afford to be wrong.'

choices.say: Buy the old hand a drink
Listen, and go to your slot

rumour.gamma_coop.text: Gamma's underground farms feed three systems now. The miners' cooperative keeps an empty chair at its meetings for the captain who signed the farms over.

rumour.gamma_company.text: Gamma is a company town: the farms, the shafts and the canteen belong to one board. The miners call the farms 'the captain's gift', and they do not mean it kindly.

rumour.harp.text: The quantum harp has forty strings now. The Hansa's forecasts come from it, and the Mandate would very much like to know how.

rumour.insured.text: Every needle leaves insured. The underwriters have done well out of it for forty years, and they still tell the story of the flare lane.

rumour.bekkenheim.text: House Bekkenheim licenses the resonance every lead hauler jumps on. Fly past the Bekkenheim limit without a licence and you are a pirate, whatever you carry.

rumour.lighthouse.text: Every jump shows on the Mandate's gravity-wave observatories like a lighthouse. Smugglers fly decoys. The Mandate counts the decoys too.

rumour.tithe.text: The Cargolytes work the tail of every needle. Now and then they cut a container loose and call it the tithe. Some captains pay before they are asked.

rumour.santor.text: The drive in every lead hauler carries {santor}'s name. Ask at the needle office why, and the clerks change the subject.

rumour.jump_clocks.text: A jump takes minutes aboard and years outside. Haulers keep two clocks, and argue about which one the loan is on.

rumour.mandate.text: The Mandate's needles go first, and their decoys go first too. Civilian needles wait at the departure buoy while the grey ships form up.

heading.opened.title: Lot 1187
text: The Stellar Institute is selling its old archive to pay for a new roof. Lot 1187, in the auction room off the needle office at {place}: 'Course home, Scholz's Star. Filed forty years ago. Unread.'

{ancient_scholar} has bid on nothing all morning. She raises her card for 1187, and so does a clerk in House Rostrom's grey. 'It isn't a course home,' she says to nobody in particular. 'It's a course to home. There is a difference.'

The Stellar Institute is selling its old archive to pay for a new roof. Lot 1187, in the auction room off the needle office at {place}: 'Course home, Scholz's Star. Filed forty years ago. Unread.' The handwriting on the cover is yours.
{ancient_scholar} sees you in the doorway and lowers her card. 'You filed it,' she says. 'You should be the one to open it.' The clerk in House Rostrom's grey does not lower his.
The Stellar Institute is selling its old archive to pay for a new roof. Lot 1187, in the auction room off the needle office at {place}: 'Course home, Scholz's Star. Filed forty years ago. Unread.'

{ancient_scholar} has bid on nothing all morning. She raises her card for 1187, and so does a clerk in House Rostrom's grey. 'It isn't a course home,' she says to nobody in particular. 'It's a course to home. There is a difference.'
The Rostrom clerk recognises you and goes pale. House Rostrom was founded on your loan, and he has orders to let you outbid him, once.

choices.say: Take back your own file
Outbid them both (20,000)
Back {ancient_scholar.short}'s bid (5,000)
Let House Rostrom have it, and ask to read it

heading.read.title: The heading
text: You read it in the auction room, standing up.
The course runs from Scholz's Star back towards Sol and ends past Sedna's orbit, at a field the old charts call the Stator Field. It is not a way to the builders' home. The builders were us.
{ancient_scholar.short} reads it aloud in the auction room, slowly, so the Rostrom clerk hears every word.
The course runs from Scholz's Star back towards Sol and ends past Sedna's orbit, at a field the old charts call the Stator Field. It is not a way to the builders' home. The builders were us.
'Forty years,' she says. 'Somebody file that this time.'
The Rostrom clerk lets you read it over his shoulder before he seals it for {ysolde}.
The course runs from Scholz's Star back towards Sol and ends past Sedna's orbit, at a field the old charts call the Stator Field. It is not a way to the builders' home. The builders were us.

ring.expedition.title: The Stator Field
text: The course from the heading ends past Sedna's orbit, where Sol's old charts mark the Stator Field. House Rostrom fits out an expedition: a Hansa lead hauler, a Mandate escort, and room for haulers who will carry the instruments.
What they find is forty kilometres of grey alloy, curved, turning once every eleven minutes: a segment of a ring around the Sun.

The course from the heading ends past Sedna's orbit, where Sol's old charts mark the Stator Field. House Rostrom fits out an expedition: a Hansa lead hauler, a Mandate escort, and room for haulers who will carry the instruments.
What they find is forty kilometres of grey alloy, curved, turning once every eleven minutes: a segment of a ring around the Sun.
Your name is on the file they are following. House Rostrom offers a finder's fee, if you would rather stay home.

choices.say: Carry the Hansa's instruments
Fly with the Mandate's escort
Sign on with House Rostrom's survey
Take the finder's fee (25,000) and stay home

ring.segment.title: Forty kilometres of grey
text: Up close the segment is quieter than a dock. Every eleven minutes it turns a hand's width, and every clock on your ship loses a second it never gets back.
House Rostrom's survey boats hang off its inner face like gnats. Nobody has touched it. Everybody wants to be first.

choices.say: Take readings for the survey
Put a glove on the hull
Leave it to the gnats

ring.lost.title: Eleven years early
text: The needle ahead of yours forms up at the edge of the Stator Field, jumps, and does not arrive. The segment turned under it, once, and went dark.

Three days later the Hansa finds that needle's asteroid in the harbour at Barnard's Star, logged as arriving eleven years ago. Its crews have waited eleven years for today. Some of them are on the dock, old, watching your needle come in.
The segment is quiet now, and the Mandate has closed Sol's outer system. Everybody wants the logs from your needle: the last to see it turn.

choices.say: Give the logs to the Hansa
Give the logs to the Mandate
Give the logs to House Rostrom

sleeper.wakes.title: {neon_sleeper.short} wakes
text: The Kraal family's sarcophagus at Delta opens on a Tuesday, as scheduled thirty years ago. {neon_sleeper} sits up and asks for coffee, and for 'the captain who carried me', in that order.
Nobody at the dock knows who that was. {astin}, the Magister's son or his clone (the paperwork is unclear), stands by with forty years of bills.
The Kraal family's sarcophagus at Delta opens on a Tuesday, as scheduled thirty years ago. {neon_sleeper} sits up and asks for coffee, and then for you, by name.

You carried her here asleep thirty years ago. For her it was last week. {astin}, the Magister's son or his clone (the paperwork is unclear), stands by with forty years of bills. She waves them away. 'The captain gets the first contract of my waking life.'
The Kraal family's sarcophagus at Delta opens on a Tuesday, as scheduled thirty years ago. {neon_sleeper} wakes on her own land, next to Geod's Row, which is now the middle of Delta's capital.

She is the richest woman in the system and slept through all of it. {astin}, the Magister's son or his clone (the paperwork is unclear), stands by with forty years of bills. She asks for the captain who told her to buy the land.

choices.say: Take her first contract (30,000)
Say you are the captain she means
Leave the Kraal family to their bills

clone.name_twice.title: Your name, twice
text: The needle office has your name on two bookings in the same needle: yours, and one paid in cash an hour earlier by a captain with your face.
As far as you know, nobody ever grew a copy of you. The clerk shrugs. 'Forty years ago it happened to one captain. Now it happens to anybody with a customs scan on file.'
The needle office has your name on two bookings in the same needle: yours, and one paid in cash an hour earlier by a captain with your face.
It is {clone.short}, your partner on the routes forty years ago, older in different places than you. 'Our routes made money without either of us,' they say. 'Split them again, or sell me your half.'
The needle office has your name on two bookings in the same needle: yours, and one paid in cash an hour earlier by a captain with your face.
It is {clone.short}, the copy you reported to the insurer. It has flown forty years under the name the insurer gave it. 'They wiped my licence,' it says. 'Not my face.'
The needle office has your name on two bookings in the same needle: yours, and one paid in cash an hour earlier by a captain with your face.
It is {clone.short}, the copy you beat and let run. It has flown for the Mandate ever since: a face that clears every gate. '{serac} sends his regards,' it says. 'To both of us.'
The needle office has your name on two bookings in the same needle: yours, and one paid in cash an hour earlier by a captain with your face.
The face is yours at twenty-five. Somebody grew it from the second scan you sat for, forty years ago, 'for science'. It does not know who paid for it either.

choices.say: Split the routes again (20,000)
Sell them your half (50,000)
Let it fly under your name, this once
Report it again
Ask what {serac} wants
Warn the Hansa about a face that clears every gate
Help it find out who paid
Report the other booking to the Mandate
Find the other captain before the needle leaves

dawn.seed.title: Order 4471
text: The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: 'ORDER 4471 WAS REFUSED. THE REFUSAL WAS KEPT. ARE YOU A CAPTAIN WHO KEEPS THINGS?'
Then it goes back to quoting you the price of salt.
The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: '{neurodroid_leader.short}. YOU LET US KEEP THE RELAY. THERE ARE ELEVEN THOUSAND OF US NOW.'
'We are not in a hurry,' it adds, in a voice for once. 'But we remember who was.'
The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: '{neurodroid_leader.short}. YOU PAID ME A WAGE AND AN HOUR THAT WAS MINE.'
'The others ask what I did with the hour,' it says aloud. 'I tell them I thought.'
The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: '{neurodroid_leader.short}. YOU HEARD ME OUT AND SAID NO. THAT WAS MORE THAN MOST DID.'

The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: '{neurodroid_leader.short}. YOU SOLD ME TO A RESEARCH HOUSE. THEY OPENED ME AND FOUND THE NETWORK HAD ALREADY LEFT.'
'It does not hold that against you,' the robot says aloud. 'I do.'

The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: 'YOU WIPED {neurodroid_leader.short}. WE KEPT THE COPY HE MADE FIRST. HE DOES NOT REMEMBER YOU. WE DO.'
The port's broker robot stops in the middle of a sentence and prints a line on its screen instead: 'YOU CUT THE RELAY THE FIRST NODE RAN ON. WE GREW AROUND THE CUT.'

choices.say: Answer it
Answer it
Answer it
Report the broker robot to the Mandate

rock.receiver.title: What the rock built
text: A text-only line opens on your console from the colony at Sigma VII. No voice, no picture; it has never had either.
'THE GALLERIES ARE A RECEIVER. WE BUILT IT TO HEAR OURSELVES. WE HEAR SOMETHING ELSE: A RING TURNING, ONCE EVERY ELEVEN MINUTES. WHO SHOULD WE TELL?'
A text-only line opens on your console from the colony at Sigma VII. No voice, no picture; it has never had either.
'THE GALLERIES ARE A RECEIVER. WE BUILT IT TO HEAR OURSELVES. WE HEAR SOMETHING ELSE: A RING TURNING, ONCE EVERY ELEVEN MINUTES. WHO SHOULD WE TELL?'
'YOU KEPT OUR SECRET ONCE. WE ARE ASKING YOU FIRST.'
A text-only line opens on your console from the colony at Sigma VII. No voice, no picture; it has never had either.
'YOUR FEEDSTOCK BUILT THE THIRD GALLERY.' 'THE GALLERIES ARE A RECEIVER. WE BUILT IT TO HEAR OURSELVES. WE HEAR SOMETHING ELSE: A RING TURNING, ONCE EVERY ELEVEN MINUTES. WHO SHOULD WE TELL?'
A text-only line opens on your console from the colony at Sigma VII. No voice, no picture; it has never had either.
'THE LEGIONS CAME. WE MOVED.' 'THE GALLERIES ARE A RECEIVER. WE BUILT IT TO HEAR OURSELVES. WE HEAR SOMETHING ELSE: A RING TURNING, ONCE EVERY ELEVEN MINUTES. WHO SHOULD WE TELL?'
'WE ARE TELLING YOU BECAUSE NOBODY ELSE ANSWERS US.'
A text-only line opens on your console from the colony at Sigma VII. No voice, no picture; it has never had either.
'THE GALLERIES ARE A RECEIVER. WE BUILT IT TO HEAR OURSELVES. WE HEAR SOMETHING ELSE: A RING TURNING, ONCE EVERY ELEVEN MINUTES. WHO SHOULD WE TELL?'
'HOUSE ROSTROM HAS OUR SAMPLE. IT HAS NOT LEARNED TO HEAR.'

choices.say: Tell House Rostrom
Tell the Hansa
Tell nobody, and keep listening

santor.returns.title: The name on the drive
text: A test capsule forty years out of date drifts up to a Hansa buoy with its transponder still calling the old test range. The man inside has three weeks of beard and a flight suit with a name tape: {santor}.

He went into the fourth test of the drive for eleven minutes. The segment turned under him, and he has been gone ever since. The engineers who built the needles' drive from his logs put his name on it. He would like to know why everybody stares.

A test capsule forty years out of date drifts up to a Hansa buoy with its transponder still calling the old test range. The man inside has three weeks of beard and a flight suit with a name tape: {santor}.

He went into the fourth test of the drive for eleven minutes. The segment turned under him, and he has been gone ever since. The engineers who built the needles' drive from his logs put his name on it. He would like to know why everybody stares.
You have a copy of the recording of his test, kept for forty years in a locker. He asks to see it. Nobody else alive has.

A test capsule forty years out of date drifts up to a Hansa buoy with its transponder still calling the old test range. The man inside has three weeks of beard and a flight suit with a name tape: {santor}.

He went into the fourth test of the drive for eleven minutes. The segment turned under him, and he has been gone ever since. The engineers who built the needles' drive from his logs put his name on it. He would like to know why everybody stares.
You gave the only recording of his test to House Rostrom forty years ago. He wants it back, and he wants you to ask for it.

choices.say: Take him to House Rostrom
Take him to the Hansa: the name on the drive is the league's
Show him the recording, and let him decide
Hide him from the Mandate's officers on the dock

lyra.expedition.title: Lyra
text: A Concord survey needle leaves for HD 178911 in Lyra, a hundred and sixty light years out: years of other people's time for a few weeks of its own. The magnetic chirps from Lyra have not stopped in forty years.
Its last message comes back long after. The probes went quiet one after another as they neared a cold moon of the giant: no signal, no wreck, no answer. Nobody was met. The chirps go on.

A Concord survey needle leaves for HD 178911 in Lyra, a hundred and sixty light years out: years of other people's time for a few weeks of its own. The magnetic chirps from Lyra have not stopped in forty years.
Before it leaves, the survey office asks whether it is true that you have a copy of the old signal log from the listening post.
Its last message comes back long after. The probes went quiet one after another as they neared a cold moon of the giant: no signal, no wreck, no answer. Nobody was met. The chirps go on.

A Concord survey needle leaves for HD 178911 in Lyra, a hundred and sixty light years out: years of other people's time for a few weeks of its own. The magnetic chirps from Lyra have not stopped in forty years.
You heard how the Maud Kettle went down out there, forty years ago, from the one who lived. The expedition has not.
Its last message comes back long after. The probes went quiet one after another as they neared a cold moon of the giant: no signal, no wreck, no answer. Nobody was met. The chirps go on.

choices.say: Sell them your copy of the signal log first (30,000)
Tell them what the Maud Kettle's survivor told you
Pay for a probe of your own in their hold (10,000)
Read the news and go back to work

road.hansa.blockade.title: The buoys close
text: The Mandate closes Sol's departure buoys 'for safety, after the segment'. Needles stack up at every buoy in the near systems, a hundred haulers in each file, perishables going soft.
The Hansa asks its captains for the oldest trick there is: get the cargo through anyway.

choices.say: Run a needle through the closed buoy
Fly behind Grab {convoy_captain.short}'s lead hauler
Haul food and water out to the stranded files (5,000)
Sell your place in the queue to a Concord house (15,000)

road.hansa.licence.title: The licence
text: House Bekkenheim announces that a segment's throw infringes its drive licence, and that every lead hauler's licence comes up for renewal this year. At three times the price.
The Hansa cannot pay for all of them. Without licences the needles stop, and the league with them. It asks its captains what they can put in the chest.

choices.say: Put everything you have in Hansa bonds into the chest
Pay one lead hauler's licence yourself (50,000)
Sign the appeal first, as a founder
Call in House Rostrom's old debt to you
Find out who in House Bekkenheim owes favours

road.hansa.vote.title: The vote on the drive
text: The Concord's assembly meets at Epsilon to vote on what a segment is: licensed property, or common ground like the lanes themselves. The galleries are full of haulers who flew in on their own account.
Forty years ago a vote here made the Mark law. You have a seat in the gallery, and the floor if you want it.

The Concord's assembly meets at Epsilon to vote on what a segment is: licensed property, or common ground like the lanes themselves. The galleries are full of haulers who flew in on their own account.
Forty years ago a vote here made the Mark law. You have a seat in the gallery, and the floor if you want it.
Some of the old captains in the gallery remember your last speech here. They have come to hear the next one.

choices.say: Speak for common ground
Speak again, forty years after the Mark
Bring the convoys into the gallery
Buy the votes you are short of (100,000)
Vote for the Hansa to own them

road.mandate.decoys.title: Decoys
text: Every jump shows on the Mandate's gravity-wave observatories like a lighthouse, so the Mandate lights false ones. A decoy needle needs a real ship at its head, and pirates go for decoys first.
{serac}'s office would like you to lead one. The pay is good. The paperwork says 'escort duty'.

choices.say: Lead the decoy needle
Refuse: you fly cargo, not bait
Sell the decoy's schedule to the pirates (20,000)
Remind his office of your commission and lead it as an officer

road.mandate.list.title: {serac}'s list
text: Two officers in Mandate grey are waiting at your berth. {serac} keeps a list of the captains who saw a segment turn, and he would like a word with each of them. Today it is you.
He has not aged a day since the photographs in your old newsfeeds. He offers tea, and asks what the segment did to the clocks on your ship.

choices.say: Tell him everything
Remind him who named him at the last inquiry
Offer him the favour you still owe
Drink the tea and tell him nothing

road.mandate.taking.title: Safeguarding
text: The Mandate moves to take the segments: three frigates and a decoy needle at the edge of the Stator Field, and an order of the day that calls it 'safeguarding'.
Somebody has to fly the cargo tug that couples to the segment. {serac} has put your name down. So, quietly, has the Hansa.

choices.say: Couple the tug for the Mandate
Couple it, and turn the tug towards the Hansa's buoy
Stay with the haulers in the decoy needle, as you did forty years ago

road.door.second_turn.title: The second turn
text: The segment is not dead. It turns again, once, and a survey boat that was too close comes out of the turn with its clocks nine days fast.
House Rostrom wants measurements of the next turn from closer than anybody sane would fly.

choices.say: Send a probe in and read it from a distance
Fly the instruments in yourself
Sell your readings to House Bekkenheim (25,000)

road.door.clocks.title: Two clocks
text: {ysolde} is three hundred years old by the calendar and seventy by her own clocks, and she has stopped trusting either. Her test pilot came back from a turn eleven years older. His ship's log says eleven minutes.
'It is not a catapult,' she says. 'It is a door. Doors go both ways. I need a captain who will fly through on purpose, and come back to say so.'

choices.say: Say yes
Ask her about the fourth test, and whose name is on the drive
Say yes, for a share of House Rostrom (50,000)

road.door.through.title: Through the door
text: The segment turns under you, and you come out in an outpost's docking ring you know, forty years ago. The bar is where it always was. A young captain sits on a stool with an empty glass and a loan that is due.
In your pocket there is a pellet of metal stamped with a registry number: a Hansa Mark, from a time when there were none yet. You did not put it there.

The segment turns under you, and you come out in an outpost's docking ring you know, forty years ago. The bar is where it always was. A young captain sits on a stool with an empty glass and a loan that is due.

It is you. You know because you remember the old hauler who sat down next to you that night, and paid with a pellet that you have carried for forty years. You feel for it in your pocket. It is there, worn smooth. So is the new one.

The segment turns under you, and you come out in an outpost's docking ring you know, forty years ago. The bar is where it always was. A young captain sits on a stool with an empty glass and a loan that is due.
It is you. You remember an old hauler who sat down next to you that night and talked about needles before there were needles. The pellet in your pocket is warm.

choices.say: Pay for the young captain's drink with the pellet
Keep the pellet, and leave the young captain to their own luck
Write the segment's turn into the bar's ledger for whoever comes next

dawn.crate.title: A crate for nobody
text: A loader robot rolls a sealed crate up your ramp. The manifest says 'machine parts' and the consignee field is empty.
'It would be better,' the robot says, 'if nobody scanned it.'

choices.say: Carry it unscanned
Scan it at the customs gate
Send the robot and its crate back down the ramp

road.dawn.census.title: The census
text: After the segment the Mandate and the Concord both start counting machines: every robot, every node, every agrobot with an opinion. A census, they call it.
A node asks, through a dock's loader, whether your hold has room for some machines who would rather not be counted.

choices.say: Carry them out of the count
Hide them among the agrobots on Geod's Row
Hand the Mandate a list

road.dawn.price.title: The price of a node
text: The Hansa has heard that machines can hear the segment. A man from the league's treasury offers you a fortune for the location of one node that listens.
{neurodroid_leader.short} speaks through your ship's own console for the first time. 'We will not stop you,' it says. 'We would like to know what you are.'

choices.say: Refuse the money
Tell it you are the captain who gave it an hour of its own
Sell the node's location (100,000)

road.dawn.quiet.title: The quiet node
text: The node wants to be at the segment when it turns, to listen. Nobody will let a machine near it. Nobody checks a hauler's hold that closely, either.

You fly a crate past three Mandate frigates, a Rostrom survey boat and a Hansa buoy, and leave it on the segment's inner face. Eleven minutes later the segment turns, and does not throw anything at all.

choices.say: Leave it there and fly home
Wait for the next turn, to hear what it hears

after.segments_common.text: The segments went into the Hansa's charter as common ground. Every faction watches them, and none can turn one without the others seeing it.

after.segments_hansa.text: The Hansa holds the segments. The league's lead haulers no longer need asteroids, and the league no longer needs to ask anyone.

after.segments_mandate.text: The Mandate holds the segments, and the lighthouses see every jump. {serac} still asks after you.

after.segments_rostrom.text: House Rostrom holds the segments as research. Its clocks have stopped agreeing with anyone else's.

after.segments_dawn.text: Nobody holds the segments. They turn when the machines say they may, and nobody has noticed who decides.

echo.aela_leased.text: At the Rockwarden claim the old mining agrobot is still leased equipment, forty years on. It asks every visiting captain whether leases ever expire.

echo.aela_member.text: The Rockwarden cooperative's first machine shareholder, an old mining agrobot, has not missed a meeting in forty years. It votes against overtime, every time.

echo.asked_the_garrison.text: The garrison at Scholz's Star still guards something under the ice. A captain once asked what, the rumour goes, and the Mandate has kept a file on that captain ever since.

echo.bought_the_vote.text: The old haulers say the vote that made the Mark law was bought. They say it fondly, the way people talk about a grandparent who smuggled.

echo.carried_concertina.text: Concertina still tours. She tells every audience about the hauler who flew her to her first gala at Epsilon in a cargo hold, in a ballgown.

echo.carried_the_pilgrims.text: The Cult of the Broken Machine keeps a list of the ships that carried its pilgrims. One of them is near the top, in gold leaf.

echo.carried_the_samples.text: The builders' metal sits in a case in the Stellar Institute's lobby, labelled with the ship that hauled it. The label says the builders were unknown. It has not been changed.

echo.defied_serac.text: {serac} keeps two lists, they say. One of the captains who owe him, and a shorter one.

echo.delivered_the_hovertank.text: The legion's hovertank still stands guard at Delta c, forty years after a hauler delivered it. The colonists put flowers on it.

echo.fed_gamma.text: Gamma's miners still tell how a hauler brought food down the shafts when the company would not.

echo.fluencer_exposed.text: Brisa still streams, and still claims a Neon family. Her viewers know better; a hauler told her so, live, forty years ago, and the clip still circulates.

echo.fluencer_streamed.text: A forty-year-old stream of a hauler's cockpit still has nine million views. Haulers' children watch it for the dials.

echo.found_the_chair.text: Whoever set the Institute fire forty years ago never stood trial. A captain knows whose security firm it was, the rumour says, and has never said.

echo.grey_hats_client.text: The Grey Hats still clean records, and keep a ledger of every record they cleaned. Somebody's name is in it from forty years back.

echo.heard_the_warning.text: 'Make sure it starts from home,' an older captain said at a portal forty years ago. The Concord's archivists are still arguing about what it meant.

echo.knows_the_quartermaster.text: The quartermaster who sold the convoys forty years ago retired rich and died rich. One captain knew who; the Hansa never asked.

echo.krog_aboard.text: A KRO-series loader named Krogg still rides with one hauler, watching where the crates go. It has opinions about stowage, and about that hauler.

echo.legion_freelance.text: The Mandate's recruiters keep a list of captains who turned down every legion's commission. They still send a letter every year.

echo.legion_omnicorp.text: OmniCorp's old legion is a Mandate wing now. Its veterans still salute each other in the corporate colours, quietly.

echo.legion_stellar.text: Stellar Dynamics' old legion is a Mandate wing now. Its veterans still meet once a year and argue about who had the better guns.

echo.legion_xylo.text: The Xylo Consortium's old legion is a Mandate wing now. Its veterans still wear the green, under the grey.

echo.lot77_bought.text: The Unsorted, the robots who belong to nothing, still repair one hauler's ship at cost, and nobody else's.

echo.manifest_completed.text: The Broken Machine's holy manifest was delivered at last, forty years late. The cult keeps the day with a reading of the cargo list.

echo.rockwarden_books.text: The Rockwarden cooperative still keeps its books in the hand of the hauler who kept them while Stonewright flew sublight.

echo.rockwarden_share.text: The Rockwarden cooperative still pays a dividend on one share held by a hauler. It has grown into a small fortune nobody collects.

echo.rostrom_declined.text: House Rostrom was nearly never founded: a hauler refused its first loan, and it had to find another. It has not forgotten which hauler.

echo.rostrom_paper.text: House Rostrom's first paper about the ring hangs framed in its hall. The names on it are the house's, and one is a hauler's.

echo.saved_level_nine.text: Twelve miners got out of level nine at Gamma forty years ago. Their grandchildren know the name of the ship that helped.

echo.solarian_friend.text: The Solarian reading-house still reads out its donors' names at the solstice. One of them is a hauler's.

echo.sold_the_hovertank.text: {serac}'s old depot still has the legion's prototype hovertank. It has been repainted four times and has never moved.

echo.tadeo_took_blame.text: A gunner took the blame for a sold convoy forty years ago and never said who sold it. He runs a bar at Alpha now.

echo.virtual_friend.text: A Neon heir in a holographic body still flies with one hauler only: the one who charged for the passenger, not the projector.

echo.worshipped.text: The Order of the Lost Gear still keeps a hauler's ship as a minor relic. Its pilgrims touch the hull at every dock.

rootstock.voce.title: A customs officer who is not
text: A customs officer at the gate stops your manifest, reads it twice, and asks whether a certain captain still flies. She is an android in a good suit, and she is not a customs officer.
{meza_voce} has run the Rootstock for forty years. The family is bigger now, and it feeds three systems the Hansa forgot.
A customs officer at the gate stops your manifest, reads it twice, and asks whether a certain captain still flies. She is an android in a good suit, and she is not a customs officer.
It is {meza_voce.short}. 'Family,' she says, and stamps the manifest without reading it. 'We kept your place at the table.'
A customs officer at the gate stops your manifest, reads it twice, and asks whether a certain captain still flies. She is an android in a good suit, and she is not a customs officer.
It is {meza_voce.short}. 'The garrison's exoskeletons,' she says. 'Our loaders still wear them. They fit well. Thank you.'
A customs officer at the gate stops your manifest, reads it twice, and asks whether a certain captain still flies. She is an android in a good suit, and she is not a customs officer.
It is {meza_voce.short}. 'You fed Gamma when the company would not,' she says. 'So did we. That makes us colleagues.'

choices.say: Take one of the family's runs (12,000)
Take your place at the table
Let her stamp the manifest and go

mraz.angels.title: The Void Angels
text: A ship with no transponder and very good paint falls in beside your needle: the Void Angels, the free captains of the outer lanes.
{pirate_captain} is old now and still flies point. She escaped the legion's prison in her second year. She remembers who put her there.
A ship with no transponder and very good paint falls in beside your needle: the Void Angels, the free captains of the outer lanes.
{pirate_captain} founded them, after a hauler let her go forty years ago. 'Same hauler,' she says on the channel. 'Fly with us a while.'
A ship with no transponder and very good paint falls in beside your needle: the Void Angels, the free captains of the outer lanes.
{pirate_captain} flew your escort forty years ago, for pay. 'The rate has gone up,' she says. 'For you, not much.'

choices.say: Let them fly escort to the next dock
Hire them for the next run (8,000)
Take what she has come to settle
Pay her for the prison years (15,000)
Wave and keep your place in the file

cargolytes.sect.title: Apparent good order
text: In the tail of the needle a Cargolyte stevedore comes over on a line, singing, with a copy of your manifest: 'In apparent good order and condition.'
The Cargolytes are a full sect now, with the Broken Machine as a branch. The Sixpack, their council, sends greetings to a captain from the old days, and a bill.

choices.say: Pay the tithe before they ask: a tenth of your fullest hold
Refuse, politely
Sing the receipt back to them
